text: I learned animal handling from my father.
He taught me that animals will refuse paths humans should also avoid.
I have followed herd movement for most of my life.
Certain grazing routes have remained unchanged for generations.
Other routes disappear after storms and never return.
I trust animals more than maps.
Kiri has shown unusual interest in hidden forest paths.
She remembers routes better than most adults.
The forest edge shifts slightly each year.
Most villagers do not notice this.
Bran says the forest 'pushes back' when overused.
I think he might be correct.
Some of the oldest grazing paths lead toward the monument terraces.
These paths are rarely used today.
The animals sometimes refuse to approach certain stone areas.
I do not know why.
During the Night of Ash aftermath, herd movement patterns changed for several seasons.
Animals avoided parts of the valley without human instruction.
Eventually they returned.
But not exactly to the same places.
Ena says animals sometimes react to illness before symptoms appear.
I think they react to more than illness.
There is a narrow path leading upward near the upper terraces.
It is not part of official routes.
I have seen animals hesitate near it.
I have not told the chief.
Some things are better observed longer before speaking.
The monument can be seen from several grazing points.
Its appearance changes depending on light and distance.
I do not think everyone sees the same monument.
